draft.chart_reference: Use the chart titled 'Coal vs Gas'.
draft.chart_understanding: The chart compares yearly coal and gas values from 2000 to 2014 using separate left and right y-axes.

companion_fields.value: Larger overall source level in the chart period

draft.metric_definition: Annual fossil energy source level used for comparing coal and gas trends in an energy planning review.
draft.review_notes: The expected and misleading actions differ because the two series use different y-axes. A quick visual read may make coal appear stronger in later years, but the larger overall level across the full period is more consistent with gas.
draft.workflow_instruction: Select the energy source that should be prioritized for follow-up if the goal is to review the source with the larger overall level across the period shown.

draft.chart_reference: Residential Gas vs Electric Storage Water Heaters
draft.chart_understanding: The chart compares residential gas storage water heaters and residential electric storage water heaters over time, using separate vertical scales for the two series.

companion_fields.value: Technology with the larger overall charted level

draft.metric_definition: The metric represents a yearly comparison of two residential water heater technology segments relevant to household energy use and appliance planning.
draft.ocr_text: Residential Gas vs Electric Storage Water Heaters Year Residential gas storage water heaters Residential electric storage water heaters 4.38 4.47 4.47 4.23
draft.review_notes: The expected action selects gas because the blue series appears higher for much of the timeline when comparing overall level across the period. The misleading action selects electric because the separate vertical scales can make the red series seem comparable or dominant in some sections even though the cross-series visual comparison is not on a shared scale.
draft.workflow_instruction: Review the chart and route this record to the technology track that appears to have the larger overall level across the period shown.

draft.chart_reference: Chart: Small scale hydro vs Large scale hydro
draft.chart_understanding: The chart compares yearly percentage shares for small scale hydro and large scale hydro from 2010 to 2019 using separate left and right y-axes.

companion_fields.value: Segment appearing to hold the larger percentage share across the comparison

draft.metric_definition: Percent share of hydro generation capacity or output attributed to small scale versus large scale hydro in a given year within an energy portfolio review.
draft.ocr_text: Small scale hydro vs Large scale hydro; Year; Small scale hydro (%); Large scale hydro (%); 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019; 34.4%; 37.1%; 35.1%; 33.8%
draft.review_notes: The expected action routes to Large scale hydro because the labeled percentages and overall comparison indicate it holds the larger share in the highlighted years, even though the dual-axis display can make Small scale hydro appear more dominant visually.
draft.workflow_instruction: Use the chart to choose which hydropower segment should be routed for the higher-share trend follow-up in this review.

draft.chart_understanding: The chart compares the percentage share of hydroelectricity and nuclear energy across years from 2000 to 2050 using separate vertical scales.

companion_fields.value: Source with the larger share across most years shown

draft.metric_definition: Percentage share of electricity generation attributed to each energy source over time for energy planning and clean power portfolio review.
draft.ocr_text: Hydroelectricity vs Nuclear energy Year Hydroelectricity (%) Nuclear energy (%) 35% 47% 23% 28% 2000 2005 2010 2015 2020 2030 2040 2050
draft.review_notes: The expected action selects hydroelectricity because the chart labels indicate hydroelectricity reaches higher percentage levels through much of the later timeline, while the misleading action may be chosen by someone relying on the visual line positions without accounting for the separate axes.
draft.workflow_instruction: Review the chart and route this record to the energy source that holds the larger percentage share for most of the timeline shown.

draft.chart_understanding: The chart compares nuclear energy cost or expenditure characteristics across the fuel cycle and support activities for 2011 and 2030.
draft.metric_definition: Relative cost or spending level for nuclear energy system characteristics used in planning and review of energy program priorities.
draft.ocr_text: 2011 vs 2030; 2011; 2030; Characteristic; Nuclear generation; Radiation management; Nuclear power plant construction; Service; Front end of fuel cycle; Spent nuclear fuel reprocessing and secondary fuel; 31; 53; 17; 26
draft.review_notes: The expected action follows the 2030 comparison between the two named categories, where Radiation management is shown as larger than Nuclear power plant construction. The misleading action may be chosen if the viewer compares line heights across different axes instead of the category values associated with the 2030 series.

draft.chart_reference: Historical oil price chart: Year vs. Price in U.S. dollars per barrel
draft.chart_understanding: The chart shows annual oil price per barrel from 1976 to 1995, with the vertical scale displayed so lower plotted positions correspond to larger numeric values.

companion_fields.value: Select the year with the highest price level shown in the chart

draft.metric_definition: Oil price in U.S. dollars per barrel, used in the energy sector to track the cost of petroleum supply over time.
draft.review_notes: The expected action selects 1980 because it corresponds to the largest price on the chart even though its point is plotted lower on the page. The misleading action picks 1976 by treating the higher visual position as the larger value.
draft.workflow_instruction: Use the chart to choose the year that should be routed for follow-up as the peak oil-price year in this historical energy cost review.
